biological.citation: Functional signatures of de novo GABBR1 and GABBR2 variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41803176)
biological.summary: Seven de novo missense variants in GABBR2 identified in individuals with autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, and/or ADHD were functionally characterized in vitro, revealing gain- and loss-of-function alterations including increased constitutive activity, reduced GABA potency, and reduced surface expression. These changes resulted in decreased GABA efficacy at the receptor, underscoring the importance of functional studies for precision medicine approaches.

biological.citation: Normalization of network activity in an epilepsy model with a constitutively active GABBR2 variant (PMID: 40994051)
biological.summary: The epileptic encephalopathy-associated GABBR2 p.I705N variant was knocked into the mouse Gabbr2 gene; heterozygous mice showed abnormal high-amplitude delta-band synchronization on EEG, increased constitutive GBR activity, reduced agonist responsiveness, and downregulation of GB1/GB2 subunits and G protein signaling components as an adaptive response. Treatment with a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-B receptors normalized spontaneous network activity, suggesting this as a therapeutic strategy for constitutively active GABBR2 variants.

biological.citation: GABBR2 mutations determine phenotype in rett syndrome and epileptic encephalopathy (PMID: 28856709)
biological.summary: De novo GABBR2 variants were identified in RTT-like patients without MECP2 mutations; variants causing milder receptor loss-of-function produced a Rett-like phenotype, while variants with more profound reduction in receptor activity produced epileptic encephalopathy. Functional rescue with a GABA-B receptor agonist was demonstrated in a Xenopus tropicalis animal model, and transcriptome-wide analysis showed GABBR2 bridges RTT- and EE-associated gene networks.

biological.citation: Development of a floxed Gabbr2 gene allows for widespread conditional disruption of GABBR2 and recapitulates the phenotype of germline Gabbr2 knockout mice (PMID: 41397015)
biological.summary: CRISPR-generated conditional knockout mice with loxP sites flanking Gabbr2, when crossed to ubiquitous Cre mice, recapitulated the global GABBR2 knockout phenotype: spontaneous epileptiform activity, hyperlocomotor activity, hyperalgesia, impaired memory, increased neuronal cell death, altered neuronal architecture, and premature death. This confirms GABBR2's essential role in neurological function and provides a tool for cell-type-specific studies.

biological.citation: GABBR2 as a Downstream Effector of the Androgen Receptor Induces Cisplatin Resistance in Bladder Cancer (PMID: 37762034)
biological.summary: GABBR2 expression in bladder cancer cells is transcriptionally regulated by androgen receptor (AR), with AR binding confirmed at the GABBR2 promoter by chromatin immunoprecipitation. GABBR2 was upregulated in cisplatin-resistant bladder cancer sublines, and knockdown of GABBR2 or treatment with the GABA-B receptor antagonist CGP46381 significantly enhanced cisplatin cytotoxicity in AR-positive cells.

biological.citation: Endothelial GABBR2 Regulates Post-ischemic Angiogenesis by Inhibiting the Glycolysis Pathway (PMID: 34422926)
biological.summary: GABBR2 was upregulated in hypoxia-treated HUVECs and in ischemic mouse hindlimb tissue. GABBR2 knockdown in HUVECs inhibited hypoxia-induced proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and decreased blood flow recovery in a mouse hindlimb ischemia model, with mechanistic evidence showing compromised glycolysis (reduced HKII, PFKFB3, PKM1 expression).

biological.citation: TAp73α drives cancer metastasis via PPI-mediated derepression of the neuronal HDAC2/REST-GABBR2 axis (PMID: 40505831)
biological.summary: Using multi-omics approaches, TAp73α was found to directly bind HDAC2, disassembling the HDAC2/REST repressor complex and aberrantly activating GABBR2 expression in melanoma cells. TAp73α-induced GABBR2 derepression upregulated EMT markers, promoted cancer cell invasiveness and proliferation, and correlated with poor survival outcomes.

biological.citation: Enteric GABAergic neuron-derived γ-aminobutyric acid initiates expression of Igfbp7 to sustain ILC3 homeostasis (PMID: 40033120)
biological.summary: GABA released by enteric GABAergic neurons inhibits ILC3 proliferation and IL-17A production via GABA receptors Gabbr1 and Gabbr2. Mechanistically, GABA suppresses the LIP isoform of C/EBP-β in ILC3s, which in turn induces Igfbp7 transcription; autocrine Igfbp7-Igf1R signaling then inhibits ILC3 activity, and this GABA-C/EBP-β-IGFBP7 pathway is suppressed in IBD patients.

biological.citation: Increased GABBR2 Expression on Cell Membranes Causes Increased Ca2+ Inward Flow, Associated with Cognitive Impairment in Early Alzheimer's Disease (PMID: 39724481)
biological.summary: GABBR2 was significantly overexpressed in brain tissues of prodromal AD patients with MCI compared to normal brains. Overexpression of GABBR2 in SH-SY5Y and BE(2)-M17 neuroblastoma cells caused increased intracellular Ca2+ concentration, elevated reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening, and increased apoptosis, implicating GABBR2 in early AD pathology.

biological.citation: HSV-1 latency-associated transcript miR-H3 and miR-H4 target STXBP1 and GABBR2 genes (PMID: 37668872)
biological.summary: HSV-1 LAT-encoded miRNAs miR-H3 and miR-H4 were shown to target GABBR2 in HEK293T cells; overexpression of miR-H3 reduced GABBR2 expression ~0.055-fold and miR-H4 reduced it ~0.687-fold. Luciferase reporter assays confirmed that miR-H3 directly targets the GABBR2 3'UTR (0.55-fold reduction) and miR-H4 also reduced GABBR2 3'UTR-driven reporter expression, suggesting viral miRNA-mediated suppression of GABAergic signaling during HSV-1 latency.
